items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: there was another drummer in there also by the name of Buster... Walter more or less wanted to be a flash drummer... you got in the band, and you played -- you just played hard.

ctx.x: Yeah, they were -- me, I was a pusher and a gouger. In other words, if I couldn't lift a band in whatever kind of beat I was playing, you know, if I couldn't dig in myself and lift that whole band, well, then I'd consider myself nothing. But I was just a hard worker.

When I went in the Army, boy standing right here in this living room by the name of Walter [Kindness.] He said; you know, when you came in the Army -- he was talking in front of his wife -- you came in to serve for me, and then you got in the band, and you played -- you just played hard. He said, that was the thing that kept me out of the band and, you know, like to go -- well, there was another drummer in there also by the name of Buster, little West Indian boy. Now, he had some nice, fast hands. He could do his…
Walter more or less wanted to be a flash drummer.
